dashboard.podcasts.title: Podcasts
dashboard.power.restartText: Music stops and this page disconnects. Open Settings › Dashboard on the Y1 again once it’s back.
dashboard.power.shutDownText: Music stops and this page disconnects. Press the Power button on the Y1 to turn it on again.
dashboard.radio.chip: The radio didn’t start. Turn it on again.
dashboard.radio.intro: Your Rondo's radio. Wired headphones are its antenna.
dashboard.radio.noSaved: No saved stations yet. Tune one in and press Save this station.
dashboard.radio.outputSub: The speaker plays out loud; the headphones stay plugged in as the antenna.
dashboard.radio.outputSubBoth: The speaker plays out loud; the headphones stay plugged in as the antenna, and they play too.
dashboard.radio.pickFrequency: Pick a frequency between {min} and {max} MHz.
dashboard.radio.plugHeadphones: Plug wired headphones into your Rondo: their cable is the radio’s antenna.
dashboard.radio.regionSub: Japan uses 76–95 MHz; most of the world 87.5–108 MHz.
dashboard.radio.scanHint: Scan to list every station your Rondo can receive.
dashboard.radio.speaker: Speaker
dashboard.server.badUrl: Enter a full address, like https://music.example.com or http://192.168.1.10:3000
dashboard.server.cantReachText: Check the address, and that the server is running.
dashboard.server.codeNeeded: Type the 6-digit code from the admin page.
dashboard.server.connectHelp: On the server’s admin page, open Device › Connect a Rondo and type the code it shows.
dashboard.server.intro: Your own Rondo server, on a computer at home or a VPS. YouTube can come through it, and WhatsApp works only through it.
dashboard.server.needsUpdateText: This Rondo needs Rondo server {version} or newer. Update it on the server’s admin page.
dashboard.server.noAccount: Search and playback work without one. Sign in on the server’s admin page for your home, subscriptions and playlists.
dashboard.server.plainHttp: Plain http: use it only on your home network.
dashboard.server.plainHttpWarn: Plain http isn’t encrypted: use it only on your home network.
dashboard.server.playbackFailed: The server’s last playback check failed. Update yt-dlp on the server’s admin page.
dashboard.server.refusedText: Replace the token with the one your server expects.
dashboard.server.rondoNoAnswerText: Keep Settings › Dashboard open on the Rondo and try again.
dashboard.server.testSub: Your Rondo calls the server and reports back.
dashboard.server.tokenHelp: For servers set up with an API token. It’s stored on your Rondo and never shown here.
dashboard.server.tokenPlaceholder: Paste the token from your server
dashboard.server.unreachable: Your Rondo can’t reach that address. Check it, and that both are on the same network for a home server.
dashboard.server.waLink: Works only through the server. Link it on the server’s admin page.
dashboard.server.waLinkOpen: Works only through the server. Link it on the server’s admin page ({link}).
dashboard.server.waNone: Works only through a server: connect one above.
dashboard.server.wrongCode: That code is wrong or has expired. Make a new one on the admin page.
dashboard.server.ytDirectSwitch: Comes directly from YouTube: you can switch it on the YouTube page.
dashboard.settings.clickSoundSub: The tick on every wheel step, separate from vibration.
dashboard.settings.date.autoSub: From the network when Wi-Fi is on. Now: {now}
dashboard.settings.date.autoZoneSub: Where your Rondo is online. Now: {city} ({zone})
dashboard.settings.date.couldntLoad: Couldn’t load the date and time. {reason}
dashboard.settings.date.dateTimeSub: Set on your Rondo, in its time zone.
dashboard.settings.intro: The screen, the wheel and the clock of your Rondo.
dashboard.settings.lyricsSub: Show the lyrics when Now Playing opens.
dashboard.settings.subtitles.showSub: When a video has them: in the language below, the video’s own track before the speech recognition’s.
dashboard.settings.subtitlesHelp: On YouTube videos and on the videos on the card, as Settings › Display › Subtitles has them on your Rondo. Hold center while a video plays to pick its track.
dashboard.settings.wheelAccelSub: Long lists scroll faster when you keep spinning the wheel quickly.
dashboard.settings.wheelVibrationSub: A short buzz on every wheel step, like Rockbox. Normal matches Rockbox’s intensity 5.
dashboard.sleep.label: Sleep timer: {state}
dashboard.sleep.title: Sleep timer
dashboard.smart.deleteText: The smart playlist goes; its songs stay on the card.
dashboard.smart.matchLine: Songs that match {select} of these rules:
dashboard.smart.newSub: Songs picked by rules: a genre, a year, what you play and rate
dashboard.smart.noMatchText: Change the rules, or play and rate more songs.
dashboard.smart.orderLine: In the order of {sort}, at most {limit} songs
dashboard.smart.summary: A smart playlist: the Rondo picks its songs by its rules.
dashboard.smart.title: Smart playlists
dashboard.sound.amplifierSub: The Y1’s own, for headphones and the speaker. Standard is the cleanest, +6 dB the loudest with more hiss.
dashboard.sound.boostSub: Louder; the peaks are held, never clipped.
dashboard.sound.deleteText: Outputs using it go back to Flat.
dashboard.sound.equalizerSub: Moving a band makes it your own (Custom).
dashboard.sound.intro: Each output keeps its own sound: the speaker, wired headphones and every Bluetooth device.
dashboard.sound.limitSub: The highest step the wheel and this page can set, on every output. Anything louder comes down to it.
dashboard.sound.matchNone: A correction for your model, from AutoEq’s measurements of about 9,000 headphones.
dashboard.sound.matchPlaceholder: Like Sennheiser HD 650 or AirPods Pro
dashboard.sound.outputSub: The one music plays on now is marked “playing”. Changes to another apply when it plays.
dashboard.sound.presetNameText: Kept with the presets, for every output.
dashboard.sound.serverOld: Your server can’t look headphones up yet: update it.
dashboard.theme.accentHelp: Colors the selection bar on the menus.
dashboard.theme.intro: Your Rondo redraws as you change things here.
dashboard.theme.locked: Settings is always in the menu
dashboard.theme.menuHelp: Show, hide and reorder the entries. Settings always stays.
dashboard.theme.previewLabel: Preview of your Rondo’s main menu
dashboard.theme.previewLong: Preview of your Rondo’s main menu: {items}. {appearance}, {size} text.
dashboard.update.installingText: Your Rondo installs it and restarts in about 15 seconds, with its settings, Wi-Fi, playlists and music as they were. This page loses it then: open Settings › Dashboard on the Y1 to come back.
dashboard.update.needsFirmware: It needs a new firmware: install it with {link}.
dashboard.update.needsUpdater: Rondo {version} needs a new firmware: install it with Innioasis Updater CE.
dashboard.update.pageBehind: The download page still has Rondo {version}. Try again in a few minutes.
dashboard.upload.cantPlay: Rondo can’t play this kind of file
dashboard.upload.noSpace: Not enough space on the card
dashboard.upload.sent: {sent} of {total}. Keep the dashboard open on your Rondo.
dashboard.upload.sentEta: {sent} of {total} · about {time} left. Keep the dashboard open on your Rondo.
dashboard.upload.skippedOne: Skipped “{name}”: Rondo can’t play that kind of file
dashboard.upload.tooBig: These files need {need} but the card has {free} free. Some will fail.
dashboard.wifi.couldntJoinName: Couldn’t join “{name}”. Check the password and try again.
dashboard.wifi.enterprise: Rondo can’t join enterprise networks like this one yet.
dashboard.wifi.forgetText: Your Rondo won’t join it on its own any more.
dashboard.wifi.forgetTextCurrent: Your Rondo won’t join it on its own any more. It’s the network your Rondo is on now, so this page will disconnect.
dashboard.wifi.leaveWarn: Your Rondo will leave “{current}”. If this phone or computer isn’t on “{name}” too, this page will lose its connection. The Rondo shows its new address under Settings › Dashboard.
dashboard.wifi.off: Wi-Fi is off on your Rondo. Turn it on under Settings › Wi-Fi on the device.
dashboard.wifi.pwShort: Wi-Fi passwords are at least 8 characters.
dashboard.youtube.accountServer: Your server has its own: sign in on its admin page.
dashboard.youtube.accountServerLink: Your server has its own: sign in on its admin page ({link}).
dashboard.youtube.codeExpired: This code expired. Get a new one.
dashboard.youtube.cookiesExpired: Signed out: YouTube no longer takes these cookies. Export them again.
dashboard.youtube.cookiesOptional: Optional: only YouTube Music’s own home and history need a cookies.txt from a browser; everything else works with the code sign-in.
dashboard.youtube.cookiesRefused: YouTube didn’t take these cookies. Export them again.
dashboard.youtube.cookiesTooBig: That file is too large to be a cookies.txt file. Export it again.
dashboard.youtube.direct: Rondo talks to YouTube itself: nothing to set up. Sign in below for Library, Subscriptions and History.
dashboard.youtube.directNoServer: Rondo talks to YouTube itself: nothing to set up. Sign in below for Library, Subscriptions and History. To go through your own server, connect one on the {link} page.
dashboard.youtube.export1: Open a private window (incognito) in your browser on a computer.
dashboard.youtube.export2: Sign in to youtube.com (or music.youtube.com: the same cookies) in that window.
dashboard.youtube.export3: Export the cookies with a cookies.txt browser extension while that page is open, then upload the file here.
dashboard.youtube.export4: Close the private window at once. If a browser keeps using that session, Google signs it out and your Rondo loses access.
dashboard.youtube.exportNote: A separate Google account for your Rondo is the safest choice. The file stays on your Rondo and this page never shows what’s inside.
dashboard.youtube.intro: Rondo gets YouTube Music and YouTube straight from YouTube, or through your Rondo server. The library on the card works without either.
dashboard.youtube.qualitySub: Auto picks up to 360p, which plays smoothest. A video without the one picked plays the next one down.
dashboard.youtube.signInCodeSub: Like signing in a smart TV: get a code, enter it at google.com/device. Brings your YouTube home, Subscriptions and History, and your YouTube Music playlists.
dashboard.youtube.signInFailed: The sign-in didn’t work. Try again.
dashboard.youtube.signedInFeeds: YouTube’s home, Subscriptions and History; YouTube Music’s playlists and Liked Music.
dashboard.youtube.step1: On your phone or computer, open {link}.
dashboard.youtube.step2: Enter the code and pick the Google account for your Rondo.
dashboard.youtube.step3: Allow access. This page updates by itself.
dashboard.youtube.tv.denied: The sign-in was refused at Google.
dashboard.youtube.tv.expired: The code expired before it was entered. Get a new one.
dashboard.youtube.tv.failed: YouTube didn’t give a code. Check the Rondo’s Wi-Fi and try again.
dashboard.youtube.tv.revoked: The sign-in was removed from the Google account. Sign in again.
dashboard.youtube.viaServer: YouTube Music and YouTube come through your server.

admin.account.changed: Password changed · other browsers are signed out

account.newNeedsAtLeast.one: The new password needs at least {count} character.
account.newNeedsAtLeast.other: The new password needs at least {count} characters.

admin.account.session: A session lasts 12 hours, then this page asks for the password again.

account.tooMany.one: Too many wrong passwords. Try again in {count} second.
account.tooMany.other: Too many wrong passwords. Try again in {count} seconds.

admin.activity.intro: The last 100 warnings and errors from the server, newest first.
admin.activity.noneText: When the server runs into a problem, such as a video that won’t resolve or cookies that stopped working, it shows up here.
admin.banner.lost: Lost the connection to the server. Trying again…
admin.brand.label: Rondo server, overview
admin.cookies.badFormat: That isn’t a cookies.txt file with youtube.com cookies. Export it again while youtube.com is open.
admin.cookies.dropOne: Drop one file: the cookies.txt you exported.
admin.cookies.empty: That file is empty. Export the cookies again.
admin.cookies.genericUntil: YouTube Music home and history are generic until you upload one.
admin.cookies.heading: YouTube Music home and history
admin.cookies.help: Optional. Only these two need a cookies.txt file from a browser; everything else works with the code sign-in.
admin.cookies.needThem: YouTube Music home, library and history need them.
admin.cookies.notCheckedYet: Not checked yet. The server checks every 15 minutes.
admin.cookies.removeText: YouTube Music home, library and history stop working on your Rondo until you upload new cookies.
admin.cookies.savedSignedOut: Saved, but YouTube says these cookies are signed out. Export them again from a new private window.
admin.cookies.saysSignedOut: YouTube says these cookies are signed out
admin.cookies.separateAccount: Use a separate Google account for the server, not your main one. Anyone with this file can use that account.
admin.cookies.sessionEnded: Google ended the session these cookies belong to.
admin.cookies.step1: Open a private window (incognito) in your browser on a computer.
admin.cookies.step2: Sign in to youtube.com (or music.youtube.com: same cookies) in that window.
admin.cookies.step3: Export the cookies with a cookies.txt browser extension while that page is open, then upload the file here.
admin.cookies.step4: Close the private window at once. If a browser keeps using that session, Google signs it out and the server loses access.
admin.cookies.subMouse: or {choose}. It goes straight to your server; this page never shows what’s inside.
admin.cookies.subTouch: Tap to pick the file you exported. It goes straight to your server; this page never shows what’s inside.
admin.cookies.tooLarge: That file is larger than 1 MB, so it isn’t a cookies.txt file. Export it again.
admin.cookies.unreadable: Couldn’t read that file. Try choosing it again.
admin.copy.addressFailed: Couldn’t copy. Select the address and copy it.
admin.copy.codeFailed: Couldn’t copy. Select the code and copy it.
admin.device.connectForToken: Connect it here to give it its own token.
admin.device.connectFromDevicePage: Connect one with a code from the Device page.
admin.device.connectText: Connect your Rondo so it can stream from this server. You’ll get a code to enter in the Rondo’s dashboard.
admin.device.disconnectText: It stops streaming from this server right away. You can connect it again with a new code.
admin.device.envNote: Your Rondo uses the token from the server’s environment (API_TOKEN) until a Rondo is connected here. Connecting gives it its own token; after that, API_TOKEN isn’t used.
admin.device.intro: One Rondo streams from this server at a time, with its own token.
admin.device.usesApiTokenServer: Uses API_TOKEN from the server’s environment
admin.error.timeout: The server took too long to answer.
admin.error.unreachableRetry: Can’t reach the server. Try again.
admin.language.label: Language
admin.offline.checkAddress: Check that the Rondo server is running and that this address is right.
admin.offline.checkRunning: Check that the Rondo server is running, then try again.
admin.offline.serverError: The server answered with an error ({code}). Check its log with docker logs y1.
admin.offline.title: Can’t reach the server
admin.overview.codeWaiting: A connect code is waiting for your Rondo.
admin.overview.connectToStream: Connect your Rondo so it can stream from this server.
admin.overview.connectedHere: Your Rondo is connected to this server.
admin.overview.encrypted: Encrypted: passwords, tokens and music travel over HTTPS.
admin.overview.plainHttp: Plain HTTP: use it only on your home network.
admin.overview.serverOut: Rondo server {version} is out. This server runs {current}.
admin.overview.thenItCan: Then it can use this server for YouTube and WhatsApp.
admin.overview.usesApiToken: Your Rondo uses API_TOKEN from the server’s environment. Connect it here to give it its own token.
admin.overview.ytdlpOut: yt-dlp {version} is out. Updating keeps playback working when YouTube changes.
admin.pair.connectedText: It streams from this server now, with its own token.
admin.pair.differentText: The Rondo connected now stops working with this server as soon as the new one connects.
admin.pair.localhost: This page is open as {host}, which your Rondo can’t reach. Use the server’s network address instead, like http://192.168.1.10:3000.
admin.pair.menuPath: Settings › Server › Connect to a server
admin.pair.replaces: Connecting a new Rondo disconnects the current one.
admin.pair.step1: On your Rondo, open {menu}, or the Server page of its dashboard ({dashboard}).
admin.pair.step3: Then enter the code. Your Rondo connects right away.
admin.password.guessable: Easy to guess: try a few random words

password.needsAtLeast.one: The password needs at least {count} character.
password.needsAtLeast.other: The password needs at least {count} characters.

admin.password.okay: Okay: a longer phrase is safer
admin.resolver.intro: yt-dlp finds the audio and video streams for each song and video. YouTube changes often: when things stop playing, update it first.
admin.resolver.lastCheckFailed: The last playback check failed. Update yt-dlp.
admin.resolver.noAnswer: no answer after 3 minutes. Check the version again in a moment
admin.resolver.nothingPlayed: Nothing has played since the server started.
admin.resolver.testText: Resolves a known video the way your Rondo does before it plays.
admin.resolver.updateText: Downloads the latest yt-dlp. It can take up to 2 minutes.
admin.setup.allDigits: Enter all 6 digits of the setup code.
admin.setup.already: This server is already set up. Sign in with its admin password.
admin.setup.codeHelp: Run docker logs y1 on the server and look for the line that starts with “Rondo setup”. The code looks like {example} and changes each time the server restarts.
admin.setup.text: Prove the server is yours with the code from its log, then choose the password for this page.
admin.setup.title: Set up your Rondo server

setup.tooManyTries.one: Too many tries. Wait {count} second and try again.
setup.tooManyTries.other: Too many tries. Wait {count} seconds and try again.

admin.setup.wrongCode: That code didn’t match. Use the code from the newest “Rondo setup” line: it changes when the server restarts.
admin.shared.codeExpired: This code expired. Get a new one.
admin.shared.insecure: Not encrypted: use it only on your home network.
admin.signin.sessionEnded: Your session ended. Sign in again.
admin.signin.text: Enter the admin password for this Rondo server.
admin.signin.tooMany: Too many wrong passwords. Wait a moment, then try again.
admin.tv.errorDenied: Access wasn’t allowed. Get a new code to try again.
admin.tv.errorExpired: That code expired. Get a new one.
admin.tv.errorFailed: Signing in didn’t work. Get a new code to try again.
admin.tv.errorRevoked: The sign-in stopped working (it was removed from the Google account). Sign in again.
admin.tv.getCodeText: Get a code, enter it at google.com/device, and the server uses that account for your home, subscriptions, history and playlists.
admin.tv.heading: Sign in with a code
admin.tv.likeTv: Like signing in a smart TV. A separate Google account for the server is safest.
admin.tv.signOutText: Your home, subscriptions, history and playlists go away on your Rondo. Search and playback keep working without an account.
admin.tv.step1: On your phone or computer, open {link}.
admin.tv.step2: Enter the code and pick the Google account for this server.
admin.tv.step3: Allow access. This page updates by itself.
admin.tv.whatYouGet: YouTube home, subscriptions and history; YouTube Music playlists and liked songs.
admin.update.alreadyNewest: The server already runs the newest image. Try again in a few minutes: the new one may still be on its way.
admin.update.carriesOn: This page carries on by itself. On a Raspberry Pi it can take a few minutes.
admin.update.keepsOld: The server keeps running the version it had.
admin.update.text: The server downloads the new version and restarts on it, which takes a minute or two. Your Rondo can’t stream until it’s back. Your settings, YouTube account and connected Rondo stay; you sign in here again afterwards.
admin.update.title: Update the server to Rondo {version}?
admin.update.tooLong: It’s taking much longer than it should. On the server, docker logs rondo-updater says why.
admin.whatsapp.codeExpired: This code expired. Cancel and get a new one.
admin.whatsapp.codeWaits: A code waits to be typed on your phone
admin.whatsapp.errorLinked: WhatsApp is linked already. Unlink it first.
admin.whatsapp.errorNoCode: WhatsApp gave no code. Try again in a minute.
admin.whatsapp.errorNumber: Type the number with its country code, like +1 555 010 0000.
admin.whatsapp.intro: Your Rondo reads and sends your WhatsApp messages through this server, which becomes one of your WhatsApp’s linked devices, as WhatsApp Web is. Link it once with a code you type on your phone.
admin.whatsapp.linkedText: Your Rondo’s WhatsApp shows your chats from here.
admin.whatsapp.numberHelp: The server asks WhatsApp for a code to type on your phone. Nothing is sent to anyone.
admin.whatsapp.numberLabel: Your WhatsApp number, with its country code
admin.whatsapp.step2: Tap Link a device, then Link with phone number instead.
admin.whatsapp.step3: Type this code. This page updates by itself.
admin.whatsapp.unlinkText: The server leaves your linked devices, and the chats and media it kept are deleted from it. Your phone keeps everything; your Rondo shows nothing new until you link again.
admin.youtube.detailNotSignedIn: Not signed in. Search and playback still work.
admin.youtube.intro: No account needed to search and play, or to open artists, albums and public playlists. Sign in for your own home, subscriptions, history and playlists.
admin.youtube.withCodeCookiesOut: With a code. cookies.txt is signed out: YouTube Music home and history are generic.

updater.connect.busy: Another program is using the Y1’s USB connection. Close the Innioasis Updater, run “adb kill-server” if you use adb, then unplug the Y1, plug it back in and try again.
updater.connect.choose: Choose the Y1 in the browser’s list…
updater.connect.disconnected: The Y1 was disconnected. Plug it back in and connect again.
updater.connect.failed: Couldn’t connect to the Y1 ({reason}). Unplug it, plug it back in and try again.
updater.connect.heading: Connect your Y1
updater.connect.noDevice: No device chosen. If the Y1 wasn’t in the list, see the tips at the bottom of this page.
updater.connect.text: Plug the Y1 into this computer with a USB-C data cable and switch it on. If it asks about a USB drive, choose Not now. Close the Innioasis Updater if it’s open.
updater.done.dark: Rondo is updated. If the Y1’s screen is dark, press a button to wake it.
updater.done.heading: Done
updater.done.running: Rondo is updated and running again, with your settings, Wi-Fi, playlists and music as they were.
updater.done.seeWhatsNew: See {link}. You can unplug the Y1.
updater.error.noFirmware: This Y1 doesn’t run the Rondo firmware yet. Install it with Innioasis Updater CE first (see the install guide), then come back for updates.
updater.error.notY1: This device is a “{model}”, not an Innioasis Y1.
updater.error.notY1Unknown: This device isn’t an Innioasis Y1.
updater.error.older: That’s an older Rondo than the one on this Y1.
updater.error.otherKey: That APK isn’t a Rondo release: it’s signed with a different key than the Rondo on this Y1.
updater.footer.license: {link} is free and open source (MIT). Not affiliated with Innioasis.
updater.footer.private: This page talks to your Y1 from your browser. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
updater.help.adb: With adb, the same update takes three commands; {link} has them.
updater.help.cable: Try another cable. Many USB-C cables only charge.
updater.help.linux: Linux: your user needs access to the device. A udev rule for USB ID 0bb4:0c03, or the plugdev group, does it.
updater.help.oneProgram: Only one program can use the Y1’s USB connection at a time. Close the Innioasis Updater, and if you’ve used adb, run adb kill-server. Then unplug the Y1, plug it back in and try again.
updater.help.title: The Y1 doesn’t show up, or connecting fails
updater.help.windows: Windows: the Y1 needs Google’s {link} (it shows up as “Android ADB Interface” in Device Manager).
updater.language.label: Language
updater.page.description: Update the Rondo firmware on an Innioasis Y1 from your browser, over USB.
updater.page.firmwareOnly: This is for a Y1 that already runs the Rondo firmware. To install Rondo for the first time, or to move from Rondo 1.0 to 2.0, use {link}.
updater.page.lead: Bring the Rondo on your Innioasis Y1 up to date from this page, over USB. It takes a minute, keeps your settings, Wi-Fi, playlists and music, and needs nothing installed on your computer.
updater.page.title: Update Rondo
updater.page.unsupported: This browser can’t talk to USB devices. Open this page in Chrome or Edge on a computer, or in Chrome on an Android phone with a USB-C cable. Or update over Wi-Fi from the Y1 itself (Settings › System › Software update) or from its dashboard.
updater.update.couldntLoad: Couldn’t load Rondo from this page. Download rondo-<version>.rondo (Rondo 2.0) or rondo-<version>.apk (1.0) from GitHub’s Releases page and choose it with “Use a file”.
updater.update.failed: Something went wrong: {reason}. Check the cable and try again.
updater.update.heading: Update Rondo
updater.update.needsFirmware: {name} needs a new firmware, so it installs with {link} instead. Rondo on this Y1 stays as it is.
updater.update.readySame: Ready: {name}. This Y1 already has it.
updater.update.waiting: Installed. Waiting for Rondo to start again…
updater.update.wantApk: This Y1 runs Rondo 1.0: choose a rondo-<version>.apk file.
updater.update.wantBundle: This Y1 runs Rondo 2.0: choose a rondo-<version>.rondo file.
